fields.value: No detailed portrait; the narrative emphasizes her animated nerves, complaints, and social performance.
Excitable, indiscreet, status-conscious, persistent, and genuinely anxious about her daughters’ futures.
To marry her daughters advantageously before the Longbourn entail leaves them financially vulnerable.
Daughter of a Meryton attorney and sister of Mrs Phillips and Mr Gardiner; married above her original social position.
Not stated; middle-aged and mother of five adult or near-adult daughters.
Comic engine and a persistent expression of the real economic pressure behind the marriage plot.
Wife of Mr Bennet; mother of the five Bennet sisters; sister of Mr Gardiner and Mrs Phillips.
Pursues marriages with little restraint, suffers the Lydia crisis intensely, and celebrates the final matches without deeper change.
Lydia: indulged favourite. Jane and Elizabeth: daughters whose courtships she publicizes. Mr Bennet: spouse who retreats into mockery.
